numeric_scope: Full dCMP 800-AO/2042-auxiliary native int3c coordinate transpose, 34 auxiliary-atom calls per pass, identical deterministic synthetic cotangent. No SCF/MP2 or public Python API changes.
source_difference: Exactly one OpenMP loop pragma: schedule(static) versus schedule(dynamic). Same fork source, compiler flags, retained libcintad, integral function pointer, reduction helper, input arrays and CPU affinity.
mechanism: jobid first enumerates auxiliary shells and then contiguous 8-shell j blocks. The triangular ish>=jsh domain and varying shell angular momenta give unequal costs. Static contiguous chunks can leave threads idle; dynamic scheduling redistributes the same work.
layout_audit: Fork uses F(pair,aux); main uses C(aux,pair). They have identical linear native memory order after transposition. Fork F-order auxiliary column slices remain F contiguous; asarray(order=F) need not copy these slices. An initial full cotangent layout conversion can remain, but this diagnostic isolates a scheduling cost without any layout/API change.

history.subject: Fix OpenMP races in integral VJP reductions
history.meaning: Removed nowait and shared-output/private-buffer accumulation overlap. Each thread accumulated privately before atomic reduction.

history.subject: Fix: Non deterministic nature of gradients with omp
history.meaning: Introduced static scheduling and the current indexed per-thread-buffer reduction helper.

safety_review: The one-line dynamic change retains thread-private accumulation, the omp-for implicit barrier, the reduction helper entry/exit barriers, and disjoint output chunk ownership. It does not restore the original race. Dynamic task assignment does change local floating-point summation order, so bitwise repeatability is relaxed; observed errors are below 6.3e-15.
recommendation: Apply only the worksharing schedule change to the isolated final native candidate. Preserve the reduction helper, source interfaces, Python layout, higher-order fallbacks, and memory strategy. Validate 1-versus-16-thread gradients, water finite difference, and full dCMP gradient in the controlled final pair.
limits: One compute node and two timing samples per schedule.
Synthetic cotangent, not the actual full AD cotangent.
Absolute native-only times differ from full-AD timings; do not claim the entire 9.37-second gap is recovered until the full calculation is measured.
The two production libcintad files differ; this test holds the fork libcintad fixed and therefore attributes its measured gain specifically to scheduling.
